title: Parent Reference → Child Object
summary: Master the core idiom of runtime polymorphism: Parent p = new Child(). Understand what the reference type controls versus what the runtime object controls.
learningObjectives: Understand the distinction between compile-time reference type and runtime object type
Identify which methods can be invoked through a parent reference (compile-time accessibility)
Understand how overridden methods resolve to the child's implementation at runtime
Learn why a parent reference cannot directly access child-specific methods without casting
expectedOutcomes: Mastery in reasoning about 'Parent p = new Child()' in complex code tracing
Understanding the exact mechanics of compiler checks versus JVM runtime execution

activities.title: Practical Context: Decoupling Caller Interfaces from Concrete Implementations
activities.content:
In professional Java architectures, code is structured around parent types rather than concrete subclasses.

When building an enterprise notification dispatcher:
- The calling service interacts with a `Notification` reference.
- At runtime, that reference can hold an `EmailNotification`, `SmsNotification`, or `PushNotification`.

This separation allows applications to manage diverse runtime entities through clean, standardized reference types.

activities.title: Reference Type vs Actual Object Type: Definition and Mechanics
Vehicle Reference Holding SportsCar Object

steps.description: Vehicle reference 'v' can invoke start() and accelerate() because they exist in Vehicle.
v.accelerate() dispatches dynamically to SportsCar's overridden method at runtime.

v.brand resolves to Vehicle's field; instance variables do not participate in polymorphism.

activities.title: Mastery Verification: Parent Reference -> Child Object (10 Questions)

questions.question: In 'Animal a = new Dog();', what is Animal called and what is Dog called?
options: Animal is the object type; Dog is the reference type
Animal is the compile-time reference type; Dog is the runtime object type
Both are reference types
Animal is the child; Dog is the parent
questions.explanation: Animal is the compile-time reference type; Dog is the runtime object instantiated in the heap.

questions.question: If class Dog extends Animal and adds a new method bark(), can we call 'a.bark()' on 'Animal a = new Dog();'?
options: Yes, because the object in memory is a Dog
No, a compile-time error occurs because bark() is not declared in Animal
Yes, if Animal is abstract
Only at runtime
questions.explanation: The compiler checks the reference type (Animal). If Animal doesn't declare bark(), compilation fails.

questions.question: If Dog overrides Animal's makeSound() method, which version runs for 'Animal a = new Dog(); a.makeSound();'?
options: Animal's makeSound()
Dog's overridden makeSound()
Both execute in sequence
java.lang.Object's method
questions.explanation: Overridden methods are dispatched dynamically at runtime based on the actual object (Dog).

questions.question: Are instance variables in Java polymorphic when accessed via a parent reference?
options: Yes, variables are overridden just like methods
No, variables are resolved at compile time based on the reference type (Variable Hiding)
Only static variables are polymorphic
Only public variables are polymorphic
questions.explanation: Instance variables are NOT polymorphic. Variable access is determined strictly by the reference type at compile time.

questions.question: Given Parent p = new Child(); where both declare 'int x = 10' and 'int x = 20' respectively. What does p.x evaluate to?
options: Compilation error
questions.explanation: p is of type Parent, so p.x accesses Parent's field (10). Fields do not participate in dynamic dispatch.

questions.question: Why is 'Parent p = new Child()' legal in Java without an explicit cast?
options: Because Child IS-A Parent (Upcasting is safe and implicit)
Because the compiler deletes the Child class
Because both classes have the same size in memory
It is only legal if Child has no methods
questions.explanation: A child class is guaranteed to fulfill all contracts of its parent class, making upcasting implicit and 100% safe.

questions.question: What happens if you write 'Child c = new Parent();'?
options: It compiles normally
Compile-time error: Type mismatch (cannot convert Parent to Child)
Runtime NullPointerException
Parent becomes a subclass of Child
questions.explanation: A Parent is NOT necessarily a Child. Downcasting without an explicit cast is rejected by the compiler.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of declaring method parameters as parent types (e.g. 'void process(Vehicle v)')?
options: The method can accept any subclass of Vehicle (Car, Truck, Motorcycle) without code changes
The method runs on a GPU
It eliminates all need for object instantiation
It prevents memory garbage collection
questions.explanation: Programming to parent types makes methods polymorphic and open to any future subclasses.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about 'Parent p = new Child()'?
options: p can access all private child fields
p is limited to members declared in Parent, but executes overridden child methods
p cannot invoke any methods
p creates two distinct objects in the heap
questions.explanation: The reference type restricts visible members, while the heap object provides the runtime implementation.

questions.question: How can you invoke a child-specific method on a Parent reference holding a Child object?
options: Using super.childMethod()
By explicitly downcasting the reference: ((Child) p).childMethod()
By declaring the method static in Parent
Child-specific methods can never be called
questions.explanation: Downcasting ((Child) p).childMethod() allows access to child-specific methods.

activities.title: Interview Essentials: Parent Reference -> Child Object

interviewQA.question: In 'Parent p = new Child();', explain what the compiler does versus what the JVM does.
interviewQA.answer: The compiler checks the reference type (Parent). It verifies that any method invoked on 'p' exists in the Parent class and that arguments match its signature. At runtime, the JVM inspects the actual object created in the heap (Child). If the method is overridden in Child, the JVM dynamically dispatches and executes Child's implementation.

interviewQA.question: Why aren't instance variables polymorphic in Java? What is variable shadowing/hiding?
interviewQA.answer: Method overriding relies on the virtual method table (v-table) in heap memory. Instance variables do not use v-tables; variable references are resolved at compile time based strictly on the declared reference type. If a child defines a field with the same name as a parent field, the child field hides the parent field, but both exist in memory.

interviewQA.question: If you have 'Object obj = new String("Hello");', why can't you write 'obj.length()'?
interviewQA.answer: Because the compile-time reference type is java.lang.Object. The Object class does not define a length() method. Even though the object in the heap is a String that has length(), the compiler blocks the call for type safety. You must cast it: '((String) obj).length()'.

interviewQA.question: What is the architectural purpose of programming to a parent reference rather than a concrete subclass?
interviewQA.answer: Programming to parent types (or interfaces) decouples client code from specific implementations. For example, a method accepting 'PaymentGateway' can process CreditCard, PayPal, or Crypto without modifying a single line of client code when new gateways are added in the future.

interviewQA.question: Given Parent p = new Child();, what will 'System.out.println(p);' output?
interviewQA.answer: It calls p.toString(). Because toString() is defined in Object and inherited by Parent, if Child overrides toString(), the JVM dynamically invokes Child's toString() method, printing Child's formatted representation.

interviewQA.question: What happens if a parent class constructor calls an overridden method when instantiated via 'Parent p = new Child()'?
interviewQA.answer: The Child's overridden method executes while Child's instance variables are still uninitialized (default 0 or null). This is a dangerous OOP pitfall that can cause subtle bugs or NullPointerExceptions, which is why calling overridable methods in constructors is an anti-pattern.

activities.title: Module 6 Lesson 5 Mastery Checkpoint
checklist: I understand what the reference type controls (compile-time member visibility)
I understand what the runtime object controls (actual method execution)
I know why p.childMethod() causes a compilation error without casting
I know that instance variables are NOT polymorphic (variable hiding)
I understand why Parent p = new Child() is safe and implicit (Upcasting)
I can predict method vs field resolution in tricky tracing puzzles
I understand how parent parameters allow generic, extensible APIs
I know how toString() dispatches dynamically on Object references
I understand why calling overridden methods in constructors is dangerous
I can explain the difference between compiler checks and JVM runtime dispatch

practiceProblems.title: Device Power-Up via Parent Reference
practiceProblems.description: Hold a Laptop instance in a Device parent reference and call powerOn().
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Call an overridden method through a parent reference:

1. Class Device:
   - Method: public void powerOn() printing 'Device turning on'

2. Class Laptop (extends Device):
   - Method: @Override public void powerOn() printing 'Laptop booting via 65W USB-C'

Test in Main:
Device d = new Laptop();
Call d.powerOn();.
hints: Declare reference: Device d = new Laptop();
Call d.powerOn(); to observe dynamic dispatch.

practiceProblems.title: Variables Bind by Reference, Methods Dispatch by Object
practiceProblems.description: Demonstrate that in Java, variables do not override (they hide), while methods override from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Demonstrate the difference between field access and method overriding from scratch:

1. Class BaseCard:
   - Field: public String type = "STANDARD"
   - Method: public String getCardInfo() returning 'BaseCard: ' + type

2. Class GoldCard (extends BaseCard):
   - Field: public String type = "GOLD" (hides parent field)
   - Method: @Override public String getCardInfo() returning 'GoldCard: ' + type

Test in Main:
BaseCard card = new GoldCard();
Print 'Field via BaseCard ref: ' + card.type;
Print 'Method via BaseCard ref: ' + card.getCardInfo();.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Field via BaseCard ref: STANDARD
Method via BaseCard ref: GoldCard: GOLD
hints: BaseCard ref.getCardInfo() dynamically dispatches to GoldCard's method ('GoldCard: GOLD').

practiceProblems.title: Database Query Engine via Parent References
practiceProblems.description: Execute SQL and MongoDB queries using a shared DatabaseConnection reference from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a database query engine from scratch:

1. Class DatabaseConnection:
   - Method: public void executeQuery(String query) printing 'Executing query: <query>'

2. Subclasses extending DatabaseConnection:
   - Class PostgresConnection: @Override executeQuery(String q) printing 'Postgres executing relational SQL: <q>'
   - Class MongoConnection: @Override executeQuery(String q) printing 'MongoDB executing document query: <q>'

Test in Main:
DatabaseConnection db;
db = new PostgresConnection(); db.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM users");
db = new MongoConnection(); db.executeQuery("db.users.find()");.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Postgres executing relational SQL: SELECT * FROM users
MongoDB executing document query: db.users.find()
hints: executeBatch(DatabaseConnection conn, String query) calls conn.executeQuery(query).
Pass instances of PostgresConnection and MongoConnection to executeBatch.

practiceProblems.title: Fix Accessing Child-Only Methods from Parent Reference
practiceProblems.description: A parent reference can only call methods declared in the parent class. Downcast to call child-specific methods.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Fix the compiler error: 'cannot find symbol openSunroof()':

Bug: `Vehicle v = new Convertible(); v.openSunroof();` fails compilation because `Vehicle` does not declare `openSunroof()`!

Your Task:
1. Call `v.drive();` through the Vehicle reference.
2. Downcast to access the child method: `((Convertible) v).openSunroof();`.

Test in Main:
Run the corrected program and verify both methods execute.
hints: Downcast v to Convertible before calling openSunroof(): ((Convertible) v).openSunroof();

practiceProblems.title: Report Exporter Dispatch Engine
practiceProblems.description: Export CSV, JSON, and XML reports using a ReportExporter parent array from scratch.
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Export reports in different formats from scratch:

1. Class ReportExporter:
   - Method: public void exportData(String data) printing 'Exporting generic data: <data>'

2. Subclasses extending ReportExporter:
   - Class CsvExporter: @Override exportData(String data) printing 'CSV Export: <data>'
   - Class JsonExporter: @Override exportData(String data) printing 'JSON Export: {"report": "<data>"}'
   - Class XmlExporter: @Override exportData(String data) printing 'XML Export: <report><data></report>'

Test in Main:
CsvExporter csv = new CsvExporter(); csv.exportData("id,name,data");
JsonExporter json = new JsonExporter(); json.exportData("Q3_Financials");
XmlExporter xml = new XmlExporter(); xml.exportData("Q3_Financials");.
hints: Pass instances of CsvExporter, JsonExporter, XmlExporter.
